Information required by the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007. A sponsor or investigator may submit a certification to delay submission of results information if they are applying for FDA approval of a new drug or device, or new use of an already approved drug or device. See Delay Results Type in the Results Data Element definitions for more information about this certification

The date on which information about a certification to delay submission of results or an extension request was first available on ClinicalTrials.gov. ClinicalTrials.gov does not indicate whether the submission was a certification or extension request. There is typically a delay between the date the study sponsor or investigator submitted the certification or extension request and the first posted date

The date on which the study sponsor or investigator first submitted a certification or an extension request to delay submission of results. A sponsor or investigator who submits a certification can delay results submission up to 2 years after this date, unless certain events occur sooner. There is typically a delay between the date the certification or extension request was submitted and the date the information is first available on ClinicalTrials.gov (certification/extension first posted)

data.Unnamed: 1: Certification/extension first submitted that met QC criteria
data.Unnamed: 2: The date on which the study sponsor or investigator first submitted a certification or an extension request that is consistent with National Library of Medicine (NLM) quality control (QC) review criteria. The sponsor or investigator may need to revise and submit a certification or extension request one or more times before NLM's QC review criteria are met. It is the responsibility of the sponsor or investigator to ensure that the study record is consistent with the NLM QC review criteria. Meeting QC criteria for an extension request does not mean that the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has determined that the request demonstrates good cause. The process for review and granting of extension requests by the NIH is being developed

In the search feature, the City field is used to find clinical studies with locations in a specific city. The Distance field is used to find studies with locations within the specified distance from a city in number of miles. For example, if you choose Illinois as the state, identifying "Chicago" as the city and "100 miles" as the distance will find all studies listing a location within 100 miles of Chicago

A research study involving human volunteers (also called participants) that is intended to add to medical knowledge. There are two types of clinical studies: interventional studies(also called clinical trials) and observational studies
Another name for an interventional study
An organization other than the sponsor that provides support for a clinical study This support may include activities related to funding, design, implementation, data analysis, or reporting
The disease, disorder, syndrome, illness, or injury that is being studied

A type of intervention model describing a clinical trial in which groups of participants receive two or more interventions in a specific order. For example, two-by-two cross-over assignment involves two groups of participants. One group receives drug A during the initial phase of the trial, followed by drug B during a later phase. The other group receives drug B during the initial phase, followed by drug A. So during the trial, participants "cross over" to the other drug. All participants receive drug A and drug B at some point during the trial but in a different order, depending on the group to which they are assigned

A group of independent scientists who monitor the safety and scientific integrity of a clinical trial. The DMC can recommend to the sponsor that the trial be stopped if it is not effective, is harming participants, or is unlikely to serve its scientific purpose. Members are chosen based on the scientific skills and knowledge needed to monitor the particular trial. Also called a data safety and monitoring board, or DSMB

A phase of research used to describe exploratory trials conducted before traditional phase 1 trials to investigate how or whether a drug affects the body. They involve very limited human exposure to the drug and have no therapeutic or diagnostic goals (for example, screening studies, microdose studies)

The key requirements that people who want to participate in a clinical study must meet or the characteristics they must have. Eligibility criteria consist of both inclusion criteria(which are required for a person to participate in the study) and exclusion criteria (which prevent a person from participating). Types of eligibility criteria include whether a study accepts healthy volunteers, has age or age group requirements, or is limited by sex
The number of participants in a clinical study. The "estimated" enrollment is the target number of participants that the researchers need for the study
A type of eligibility criteria. These are reasons that a person is not allowed to participate in a clinical study

A way for patients with serious diseases or conditions who cannot participate in a clinical trial to gain access to a medical product that has not been approved. Also called compassionate use. There are different expanded access types

Available: Expanded access is currently available for this investigational treatment, and patients who are not participants in the clinical study may be able to gain access to the drug, biologic, or medical device being studied
No longer available: Expanded access was available for this intervention previously but is not currently available and will not be available in the future
Temporarily not available: Expanded access is not currently available for this intervention but is expected to be available in the future
Approved for marketing: The intervention has been approved for use by the public
An arm type in which a group of participants receives the intervention/treatment that is the focus of the clinical trial

In certain circumstances, a sponsor or investigator may request an extension to delay the standard results submission deadline (generally one year after the primary completion date). The request for an extension must demonstrate good cause (for example, the need to preserve the scientific integrity of an ongoing masked trial). All requests must be reviewed and granted by the National Institutes of Health. This process for review and granting of extension requests is being developed. See Delay Results Type in the Results Data Element definitions for more information

A type of intervention model describing a clinical trial in which groups of participants receive one of several combinations of interventions. For example, two-by-two factorial assignment involves four groups of participants. Each group receives one of the following pairs of interventions: (1) drug A and drug B, (2) drug A and a placebo, (3) a placebo and drug B, or (4) a placebo and a placebo. So during the trial, all possible combinations of the two drugs (A and B) and the placebos are given to different groups of participants

A type of eligibility criteria that indicates whether eligibility to participate in a clinical study is based on a person's self-representation of gender identity. Gender identity refers to a person's own sense of gender, which may or may not be the same as their biological sex
A group or subgroup of participants in an observational study that is assessed for biomedical or health outcomes

A group of people who review, approve, and monitor the clinical study's protocol. Their role is to protect the rights and welfare of people participating in a study (referred to as human research subjects), such as reviewing the informed consent form. The group typically includes people with varying backgrounds, including a community member, to make sure that research activities conducted by an organization are completely and adequately reviewed. Also called an institutional review board, or IRB, or an ethics committee
A type of eligibility criteria. These are the reasons that a person is allowed to participate in a clinical study
A process used by researchers to communicate to potential and enrolled participants the risks and potential benefits of participating in a clinical study
The document used in the informed consent or process

The general design of the strategy for assigning interventions to participants in a clinical study Types of intervention models include: single group assignment, parallel assignment, cross-over assignment, and factorial assignment

A process or action that is the focus of a clinical study. Interventions include drugs, medical devices, procedures, vaccines, and other products that are either investigational or already available. Interventions can also include noninvasive approaches, such as education or modifying diet and exercise

A type of clinical study in which participants are assigned to groups that receive one or more intervention/treatment (or no intervention) so that researchers can evaluate the effects of the interventions on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The assignments are determined by the study's protocol. Participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions

A type of clinical study in which participants are assigned to groups that receive one or more intervention/treatment (or no intervention) so that researchers can evaluate the effects of the interventions on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The assignments are determined by the study's protocol. Participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions

A clinical trial design strategy in which one or more parties involved in the trial, such as the investigator or participants, do not know which participants have been assigned which interventions. Types of masking include: open label, single blind masking, and double-blind masking

A unique identification code given to each clinical study record registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. The format is "NCT" followed by an 8-digit number (for example, NCT00000419). Also called the ClinicalTrials.gov identifier
An arm type in which a group of participants does not receive any intervention/treatmentduring the clinical trial

A type of clinical study in which participants are identified as belonging to study groups and are assessed for biomedical or health outcomes. Participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to a specific interventions/treatment

The general design of the strategy for identifying and following up with participants during an observational study. Types of observational study models include cohort, case-control, case-only, case-cross-over, ecologic or community studies, family-based, and other

An adverse event that is not a serious adverse event, meaning that it does not result in death, is not life-threatening, does not require inpatient hospitalization or extend a current hospital stay, does not result in an ongoing or significant incapacity or interfere substantially with normal life functions, and does not cause a congenital anomaly or birth defect; it also does not put the participant in danger and does not require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the results listed above

For clinical trials, a planned measurement described in the protocol that is used to determine the effect of an intervention/treatment on participants. For observational studies, a measurement or observation that is used to describe patterns of diseases or traits, or associations with exposures, risk factors, or treatment. Types of outcome measures include primary outcome measure and secondary outcome measure

A type of intervention model describing a clinical trial in which two or more groups of participants receive different interventions. Established in 1989, Singhi Advisors is a global investment banking firm headquartered in Mumbai, India. Singhi Advisors caters to the industries of power equipment, engineering, infrastructures, energy, textile, apparel, information technology, logistics, chemicals, media, and entertainment.

Founded in 1856, Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken is a commercial banking firm headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden. The firm offers financial advice and a wide range of financial services to different customer segments. The firm offers corporate finance services such as acquisition finance, asset finance, corporate finance, debt capital markets, export finance, loan origination, loan syndication and loan agency, project finance, real estate finance, and shipping finance. The firm's activities comprise mainly banking services, but it also carries out life insurance operations and also owns Eurocard. The firm also offers advisory services and assists customers with financing, investments, secure payments, asset management, economic development, and international trade.

Founded in 1889, Slaughter and May is a law firm headquartered in London, United Kingdom. The firm provides services in private equity, mergers, acquisitions, privatizations, joint ventures, capital markets, debt and equity, demergers, reorganizations, corporate governance, capital raising, loan finance, and arbitration. Slaughter and May caters to aerospace, automobiles, parts, consumer goods, financial institutions, media, mining, minerals, oil, gas, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare, real estate, technology, telecommunications, transport, and logistics sectors.

Founded in 2005, Solebury Capital Group is a financing advisory firm based in New Hope, Pennsylvania. The firm advises corporates, financial sponsors, and venture capital clients. Solebury's corporate services include initial public offering, direct listing, market follow-on, special purpose acquisition companies, and block trading advisory.

Established in 1995, Sorainen is a law firm based in Tallinn, Estonia. The firm provides services in the areas of mergers and acquisitions, private equity, corporate, banking, capital markets, intellectual property, privatization, restructuring, insolvency, government relations and administrative law, and dispute resolution. The firm also caters to industries including communications, media and technology, energy and utilities, financial services and insurance, food, agriculture and forestry, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, real estate, and construction.

Founded in 2013, Sory@Law is a law firm based in Accra, Ghana. The firm offers legal services in the areas of labor, industrial relations, banking, finance, corporate finance, securities, administration of the estate, probate, mergers, acquisition, telecommunications law, intellectual property, construction law, immigration, arbitration, mediation, and negotiations.

Spreds is an FSMA-authorized investment crowdfunding platform focusing on European startups and growing businesses. Based in Brussels, Belgium, and founded in 2011, the firm enables entrepreneurs to co-invest with professional investors in startups and scale-ups across Europe.

Founded in 2012, Stanbic IBTC Capital Limited (Stanbic IBTC Capital) is an investment banking franchise in Nigeria offering a complete suite of innovative advisory, capital markets, and debt arranging solutions to domestic corporates, multinationals, and government entities operating in and outside Nigeria. The firm has a dedicated team of investment banking specialists that leverage deep industry insights across various industry sectors to deliver innovative solutions that drive business and economic growth in Nigeria. The firm is registered with the Securities & Exchange Commission as an Issuing House and Underwriter, and the FMDQ Securities Exchange Limited as a Registration Member Listings and Quotations. The firm is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Stanbic IBTC Holdings PLC (Stanbic IBTC), an end-to-end financial services company listed on The Nigerian Exchange, and a member of Standard Bank Group.

Established in 1861, Standard Bank of South Africa is a commercial bank headquartered in Johannesburg, South Africa. The bank provides personal and business banking services which include loans, overdrafts, savings and investments, insurance, mobile banking, and business mortgage services. The firm also provides self-service banking, insurance, wealth and investment services, and financial planning services.

Founded in 1853, Standard Chartered is a leading international cross-border bank serving companies and consumers through its global network The firm's activities include corporate relationship banking, leveraged finance and high yield, infrastructure and project finance, corporate real estate advisory and financing, cross-border mergers and acquisitions and structured export finance.

Founded in 2013, Stanivuk & Manasijevski is a law firm based in Belgrade, Serbia. The firm's practice areas include economy, mergers, and acquisitions, real estate, bankruptcy and restructuring, intellectual property, media law, tax, dispute resolution, labor law, banking and finance, pharmaceutical, and healthcare.

Founded in 2015, Startup Network is a crowdfunding platform based in Delaware. The firm offers a professional network for participants in the venture market, bringing together startups, private investors, and professional consultants. The offerings of Startup Network vary from pre-seed, seed, and venture capital, to business loans and business sales.

Founded in 2005, Stek Advocaten is a law firm headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The firm provides services in competition law, regulatory matters, dispute resolution, financing, mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, initial public offerings, private equity, venture capital transactions, restructuring, bankruptcy, and management buyouts. Stek caters to industries including healthcare, technology, aviation, transportation, education, consumer products and services, real estate, energy and utilities, food and beverages, and infrastructure.

Step Advisory is a boutique management consulting firm focused on fuelling business growth. The firm provides competitor and driver analysis, market segmentation, corporate dashboarding, strategy formulation and activation, organic and acquisitive growth, talent sourcing, and flexible resourcing services. Founded in 2008, Step Advisory is based in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Founded in 1890, Stifel Financial is a full-service wealth management and investment banking firm headquartered in Saint Louis, Missouri. Through its wholly-owned subsidiaries, the firm provides securities brokerage, trading, investment advisory, and related financial services to individual investors, professional money managers, businesses, and municipalities. Stifel Financial caters to healthcare, education, financial services, defense, and commercial products, among other industries.

Established in 2007, StratLink is a dynamic financial advisory firm with a deep focus on emerging markets. With strategically located offices in Nairobi (Kenya), Dubai (United Arab Emirates), and Karachi (Pakistan), StratLink is at the forefront of facilitating financial and strategic growth across the pivotal regions of Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The firm is renowned for its comprehensive suite of services, which includes expert guidance in mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, equity and debt financing, and divestiture processes, catering primarily to companies operating within these vibrant markets.
Beyond its core financial advisory services, StratLink delivers a broad spectrum of strategic solutions designed to accelerate business growth and enhance market positioning. These services encompass growth and market entry strategy formulation, strategic and operational planning, meticulous due diligence, the establishment of strategic alliances, and the creation of detailed budget forecasts. Additionally, StratLink's expertise extends to market research and business intelligence, providing clients with insightful analysis and actionable intelligence crucial for making informed business decisions and navigating the complexities of emerging markets.

Founded in 1983, Silicon Valley Bank is a commercial bank headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The bank offers online banking services, deposits, payments, and fraud prevention services. In addition, the bank also offers investments and asset management services, credit solutions and commercial card programs, and strategic advisory services, such as deal sourcing, benchmarking strategic valuations, and transaction support.

data.Unnamed: 2: Founded in 2002, Synergy Consulting Infrastructure & Financial Advisory Services is a financial advisory firm headquartered in Reston, Virginia. The firm provides services in the areas of energy, information technology, energy, utilities, agriculture, software, and other business products and services.

Established in 1990, Tahoun & Associates is a law firm headquartered in Cairo, Egypt. The firm acts on companies and procedural matters, contracts, arbitration, litigation, due diligence, labor law, insolvency, restructuring, and legal translation. Tahoun provides legal opinions on a wide range of company matters, including international trade contracts and disputes, constructions, IT, IP, and documents for establishing company branches, subsidiaries, or international corporate structures. The firm also offers legal advice for tax, social insurance, and other procedural matters. Tahoun caters to industries including aviation, financial services, construction, infrastructure, healthcare, manufacturing, real estate, technology, media, telecommunications, hospitality, and tourism.

Founded in 2008, Tamela is a financing advisory firm headquartered in Sandton, South Africa. The firm provides corporate finance advisory to merger and acquisition transactions, capital raising whether debt or equity, black economic empowerment, debt capital markets, balance sheet restructuring, mezzanine, and equity transactions, and sponsor services. Tamela has experience in a number of industries, especially the industrial, manufacturing, and financial services sectors, healthcare, and logistics.

Founded in 2002, Taylor Wessing is a full-service international law firm headquartered in London, United Kingdom. The firm offers counsel in the areas of corporate crime, mergers, acquisitions, dispute resolutions, employment, pensions, and private equity. Taylor Wessing caters to industries including automotive, consumer, retail, energy, financial institutions, healthcare, technology, media, communication, hotels, leisure, life sciences, and real estate.

Established in 1995, Templars is a law firm headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria. The firm provides legal services in mergers and acquisitions, project finance, corporate and commercial law, taxation, dispute resolution, intellectual property, and competition law. Templars caters to banking and finance, energy, natural resources, media, entertainment, technology, telecommunications, maritime, and aviation sectors.

Founded in 2011, Teneo Holdings is an independent financing advisory firm headquartered in New York City, New York. The firm specializes in financing advisory and management consulting while offering services in the areas of business transformation, restructuring, insolvency, bankruptcy, litigation, mergers, acquisitions, debt, valuation, corporate, marketing, and analytics strategy, people advisory, risk advisory, ESG, strategy, and communications. Teneo Holdings caters to clients in the life sciences, cybersecurity, industrials, infrastructure, artificial intelligence, machine learning, e-commerce, fintech, and manufacturing sector industries among others.

TerraProtein Equity Partners is a financial advisory firm headquartered in Leiden, Netherlands. The firm provides advisory services for agriculture and agri-technology investment projects within venture capital, private equity, and debt capital markets. TerraProtein Equity Partners caters to sectors like food, agriculture, and agri-technology.

Established in 2007, The New Practice is a law firm based in Lagos, Nigeria. The firm practices in the matters of private equity, mergers, acquisitions, capital raising, private equity fund, compliance, public offerings, private placements, restructuring, set-up, dispute resolution, equity, debt, and tax advisory. TNP caters to fast-moving consumer goods, oil, gas, banking, energy, natural resources, finance, financial technology, technology, e-commerce, media, telecom, infrastructure, construction, and real estate.

Founded in 1994, The Williams Capital Group was a full-service investment banking firm serving institutional investors, corporations and governments. The firm offered equity research, share repurchase, fixed income and equity underwriting, business valuations, due diligence assistance, financial modeling and investment advisory to its clients. The Williams Capital Group is headquartered in New York City, New York. The firm caters to sectors like energy, financial services, healthcare, and consumer products among others. On, 4th Nov The Williams Capital Group got merged with Siebert Cisneros Shank & Co.

Founded in 2005, Themis Law Chambers is a Law Firm headquartered in Cape Town, South Africa. The firm provides services in the areas of corporate and commercial law, mergers and acquisitions, arbitration and mediation, company secretarial, property law, labor law, and notarial services. The firm caters to individuals, the real estate sector among other sectors.

Established in 2014, Thinkroom Consulting is a management consultancy firm, headquartered in Olifantsfontein, South Africa.The firm partners with small and big businesses across Africa. Services provided by the firm include running entrepreneurship programs, development supply chains, program design, program implementation, sourcing entrepreneurs, primary or secondary research, digital marketing, and partner linkages. Thinkroom Consulting caters to financial services and information technology sectors.

Founded in 1928, Transpecos Banks is a commercial banking firm based in San Antonio, Texas The firm offers services such as deposits, credit and debit cards, money market instruments, online banking, pubic financing, paycheck protection program, loans, and mortgage services.
Founded in 2013, TruCrowd was a crowdfunding platform headquartered in Schaumburg, Illinois. On 2nd January 2025, the firm ceased operations.

Established in 2004, Tugendhaft Wapnick Banchetti & Partners is a law firm headquartered in Sandton, South Africa. The firm provides corporate, mergers and acquisitions, asset financing, debt, private equity, and insolvency law services. Tugendhaft Wapnick Banchetti & Partners caters to wholesale, logistics, automotive, real estate, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, insurance, medical records, and infrastructure industries.
Founded in 2012, Tunisian American Enterprise Fund is a private equity firm based in Tunis, Tunisia.
Founded in 2007, Ture Invest is a lender headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden. The firm provides services for performing, non-cyclical senior secured lending.

Founded in 2012, U-Start was a professional advisory firm headquartered in Milan, Italy. The firm specialized in focus areas such as lifestyle, tech, and digital companies. U-Start catered to family offices and funds on venture deals and works alongside corporates on startup scouting and innovation projects.

Founded in 1983, UUBO is a full-service corporate and commercial law firm headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria. The firm provides legal advice in aviation, intellectual property, banking and finance, mergers and acquisitions, restructuring, capital markets, dispute resolution, real estate, tax, employment, fintech, telecommunications, media and technology, and so on.

Founded in 2010, Ulule is a crowdfunding platform headquartered in Paris, France. The firm provides services for crowdfunding, fundraising, culture, innovation, crowdsourcing, social business, collaborative economy, empowerment, funding, new products, crowdfunding, arts, brands, social networks, local, global, and impact.

Founded in 1965, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is a law firm headquartered in New York City, New York. The firm practices in matters of corporate, litigation, restructuring, finance, tax, executive compensation and benefits, antitrust, strategic investments, and real estate mergers and acquisitions. WLRK caters to clients in the finance, insurance, media, high-technology, energy, industrial, consumer, retail, and real estate sectors, among others.

Founded in 1780, Wedlake Bell is a law firm headquartered in London, United Kingdom. The firm offers legal services in focus areas such as construction, finance, real estate, private client, planning and environmental, banking, pensions and employee benefits, insolvency and restructuring, employment, projects, and infrastructure, business services, and dispute resolution.

Founded in 2011, Wefunder is a San Francisco, California-based crowd-investing platform. The firm connects startups with investors online enabling unaccredited investors to purchase equity in early-stage private companies. Wefunder caters to an array of industries including technology, food, beverages, hardware, software, entertainment, retail, energy, financial services, consumer services, business services, and infrastructure among others.

Founded in 1984, Wells Fargo Securities is an investment banking firm headquartered in San Francisco, California. Wells Fargo Securities is the trade name for the corporate banking, capital markets, and investment banking services of Wells Fargo & Company and its subsidiaries. The firm assists corporate, government, and institutional clients to meet their capital, financial, banking, and investment needs. The firm provides services in corporate banking, asset-based financing, capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, market risk management, and foreign exchange among other areas.

Founded in 1917, Werksmans Attorneys is a law firm based in Sandton, South Africa. The firm provides legal services to clients on matters concerning banking and finance, arbitration, business crimes and investigations, mergers and acquisitions, data privacy, cybercrime, investment funds, private equity, and intellectual property. Werksmans advises clients across domains such as agriculture, forestry, fishing, construction, infrastructure, consumer goods, and energy.

Wholesale Investor is a private investment platform directly connecting high net-worth and professional investors with private, and small-cap listed investment opportunities that are often not available on the open market. WI offers companies direct exposure to active investors and deal makers. Wholesale Investor was founded in 2008 and is based in Sydney, Australia.

Established in 1993, Wildeboer Dellelce is a law firm based in Toronto, Ontario. The firm offers advisory services in the areas of corporate finance, mergers, acquisitions, tax, debt products, structured finance, corporate governance, and commercial real estate. Wildeboer caters to clients in the areas of blockchain, cryptocurrency, fin-tech, cannabis, esports, financial services, industrial and consumer goods, life sciences, mining, natural resources, and real estate technology.

Founded in 1923, Wildgen has remained an independent law firm, able to offer innovative and pragmatic services tailored to the requirements of each client. Excellence, client care and common sense guide the approach of the firm and its lawyers. Wildgen acts as a one-stop-shop, offering assistance in all areas of business law including banking and finance, corporate and M&A, data protection, dispute resolution and litigation, employment, energy, insurance and reinsurance, investment funds, intellectual property, technology, media & telecommunication, private equity & venture capital, real estate, sustainable finance, transport and tax. Wildgen's legal experts advise domestic and international companies, from small and medium-sized companies to multinational businesses, as well as law firms seeking advice on Luxembourg law for their clients.

Founded in 1888, Willkie Farr & Gallagher is an international law firm headquartered in New York City, New York. The firm's primary practice areas include mergers, acquisitions, private equity, business reorganization, restructuring, complex litigation, compliance, enforcement, antitrust, competition, asset management, insurance, and reinsurance. Willkie also provides integrated, multidisciplinary advice encompassing the areas of capital markets. communications and media, cybersecurity and privacy, environment, health and safety, executive compensation and employee benefits, finance, government relations, intellectual property, real estate, special committee, structured finance, tax, and various industries.

Founded in 2004, WilmerHale is an independent law firm headquartered in Washington, District of Columbia. The firm offers services in administrative law, capital markets, corporate governance, emerging companies, international trade, investment, market access, litigation, labor, employment, white-collar defense, and investigations. The firm additionally offers transaction advisory services on mergers, acquisitions, debt finance, private placements, spin-offs, carve-outs, cross-border offerings, initial public offerings, follow-on public offerings, private investment in public equity placements, venture, and strategic financing.

Founded in 2000, Worldwide Securities was an investment banking firm headquartered in Accra, Ghana. The firm provided services for corporate restructuring and privatization, divestiture design and implementation.

XSML is an investment fund manager focused on operating in frontier markets in Central and East Africa.The company offers a combination of debt & equity, typically invested as growth capital. The firm seeks to serve companies related to business, education, healthcare, service, communication and technology sectors. Founded in 2008, XSML is based in Amsterdam, Netherlands and has USD 65 million under management.

Founded in 2000, Young America Capital is an investment bank based in Mamaroneck, New York. The firm provides expertise in investment banking, asset management, public and private placement of equity and debt, fairness opinions, as well as cross-border and multinational transactions. The firm offers assistance in the areas of sales, acquisitions, divestitures, and management buyouts. YAC seeks to provide services in the consumer and retail, life sciences and healthcare, maritime, infrastructure, and logistics sectors.
